title: I Used the Beekeeping Smoker Checkout on the Treasurer Who Took Two

parts.text: I opened the equipment shed at 8:22 a.m. and smokers 1 and 2 were gone under treasurer Cole's initials twice. The board said: ONE SMOKER PER APIARY VISIT. SIGN BOTH WAYS. I was forty-five, hive volunteer, holding an empty hook. Cole was already at hive 4 with two cans. "Treasurers are the smoke." I photographed the double initials, the board, and both cans. Then I logged a double-out. At 8:31 the apiary chair asked why Cole's name was on two smokers. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The apiary chair can see Cole's initials twice on two signed-out smokers.

social.video_title: The treasurer signed out two smokers on a one-can board — Part 1/2
social.description: Beekeeping club, empty hooks, and a board he wrote. I logged the double. Would you have photographed the cans?

parts.text: Cole called it wind until the chair asked for the log. I printed the double, the photo, and the board. One can came back. Cole smoked with one and told volunteers wind was always about optics. Optics is a word treasurers use when a second can exists. Checkout now has a second line: TREASURERS ARE NOT TWO. I keep smoker 1. Cole signs once. The shed finally looks like gear, not a stash. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Double-out log, returned can, and a second line. Was wind ever two smokers?
